newsitem.title: USA: CME boneless beef contracts seen starting June 16.
newsitem.headline: CME boneless beef contracts seen starting June 16.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange's new boneless beef and boneless beef trimmings contracts are expected to have their inaugural starting day on June 16, if the CME board of directors approves it next week, a CME spokesman said.
The new contracts will trade in the live cattle futures pit and have the same trading months and expiration days as live cattle.

However, trading hours will be 0850 CDT/1350 GMT to 1300 CDT/1800 GMT instead of live cattle's 0905 CDT/1505 GMT to 1300/1900 GMT time frame. Boneless beef will have a ticker symbol of BB and trimmings TR.
The first month of trading for the cash-settled contracts will be August 1997 if the board approves, The spokesman said.

The 90 percent lean boneless beef and 50 percent boneless beef trimmings will have a minimum price fluctuation of .10 cent a lb and a daily price limit of 3.00 cents a lb. Limits will be expanded to 4.50 cents after a two-day limit move, up or down. There are no trading limits the last five days of trading.

Final settlement of the 90 percent boneless beef contract will be cash-settled to a five-day weighted average of the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Omaha and East Texas-Oklahoma cash beef prices. The 50 percent boneless beef settlement will only be on USDA's Omaha cash beef prices.
The initial day starting time will be announced later.
